name: Adaptive comparators for PAC-h: BACC-style budget pacing and theorem-matching ACI
status: written after the published PAC-h results were reproduced (regression check only) and before any comparator was run on calibration or test days
environment: same closed-loop replay as PAC-h (pac_window_grid.load/evaluate semantics): capacity at minute t is the decision issued at t-tau using data through t-tau-1; overload if demand > mu*capacity; cost = (capacity sum + 0.05 churn + 10 overload minutes)/observed-or-clairvoyant denominator; persistence forecasts for every controller
primary_cell: tau=1, delta=0.01; compliance = per-unit test overload fraction <= delta

ACI-G.description: adaptive conformal inference (Gibbs & Candes 2021) with delayed feedback handled by tau+1 interleaved ACI sequences; score = signed (tau+1)-step persistence residual; quantile = order statistic of the last W scores at rank ceil((W+1)(1-alpha_t)); alpha_t<=0 or rank>W -> infinite margin (capacity M_u); alpha_t>=1 -> empty set (margin -inf, capacity 1, miscoverage counted as 1); no clipping
ACI-G.update: alpha_{j} = alpha_{j-tau-1} + gamma*(alpha_star - err_{j-tau-1}), err = 1{y > forecast + margin}
ACI-G.target: alpha_star = delta - (1+gamma)(tau+1)/(gamma*T), with T the length of the evaluated period; this makes the deterministic finite-horizon ACI bound imply overload fraction <= delta for every unit whenever no overload occurs at capacity M_u
ACI-G.gamma_selection: per trace and budget, on calibration days with tau=0 and alpha_star computed for the calibration period: only gamma with alpha_star>0; choose most units within budget, ties by lower mean calibration cost (same rule as the PAC-h window); evaluated once on test with alpha_star recomputed for the test T and tau
ACI-G.window: W = PAC-h pre-test window for the same trace and budget
ACI-G.M_u: max(1, ceil(2 * max demand before the evaluated period / mu)); report saturated minutes and overloads in them

ACI.description: same as ACI-G but alpha_star = delta and gamma = 0.005 (Gibbs & Candes default); long-run calibration only, no finite-horizon target

BACC-r.description: re-implementation of BACC (Liu et al., arXiv:2606.20575v2) from the paper text with its published defaults; no tuning
BACC-r.mapping: one accounting unit per minute; violation = overload minute; epsilon = delta; accounting period T = evaluated test period of the unit; profile is a step at mu so lambda_safe = mu and x = max(1, ceil(y_tilde_max/mu)); startup delay d = tau

parameters.c: mu of the unit (one replica of capacity)

BACC-r.score: s_k = (y_max + c)/(yhat_max + c) over the service window of h minutes starting d minutes after the decision; added when the window completes
BACC-r.rank: j = min(m, ceil((m+1)(1-a_k))), q = s_(j); q = 1 if no score
BACC-r.pacing_and_ceiling: Eqs. (9)-(12) of the paper with minute units; A_k = sum over minutes with plans of the plan's a; i=1 minutes are those whose demand exceeded the calibrated demand of the plan in force
BACC-r.trigger: each non-regular minute: if demand exceeds the calibrated demand of the plan in force and any of the latest, rolling or cumulative violation rates exceeds epsilon, issue max(current target, ceil(((y_early + c) q - c)/mu)) with y_early = y + (1+d) max(y - y_prev, 0); increase only
BACC-r.warm_start: score history pre-filled from the 720 minutes before the evaluated period; pacing and budget state start at the period start
BACC-r.sensitivity: BACC-r with h=1 (decision every minute), labelled as a sensitivity

reporting: all cells reported regardless of direction: units within budget, mean and median relative cost, paired per-unit comparison with PAC-h (units where both comply: cost ratio), saturation counts for ACI variants; deviations listed
not_done: no comparator parameter is changed after test results are seen; any later change is a labelled post hoc analysis
